lines.text: An empire of the Wolof, an island of sorrow, a poet president and one of Africa's steadiest democracies. This is the story of Senegal.
In the fourteenth century, the Wolof people were united in the Jolof Empire, which ruled much of the land for two hundred years.
From the fifteenth century, the small island of Goree off the coast became a station of the slave trade. Today it is a place of memory.
In 1659 France founded Saint-Louis at the mouth of the Senegal River, which became the colonial capital.
Amadou Bamba, born in 1853, founded the Mouride brotherhood, a Sufi movement that still shapes life in Senegal.
In 1857 the French set up a post on the Cape Verde peninsula, the westernmost point of mainland Africa. It grew into Dakar.
From 1895 Dakar was the seat of French West Africa, a federation of colonies across the region.
Leopold Sedar Senghor, born in 1906, became a celebrated poet, and would lead his country to independence.
Ousmane Sembene, once a docker and a soldier, turned to novels and film, and is called the father of African cinema.
Born the same year, Cheikh Anta Diop became one of the great historians of Africa.
Abdoulaye Wade, born in 1926, would lead the opposition for decades, and become president in 2000.
Abdou Diouf, born in 1935, would follow Senghor as president and serve for almost twenty years.
In 1944, at Thiaroye, French troops shot African soldiers just back from the war who had asked for their pay.
Youssou N'Dour, born in Dakar in 1959, would carry the mbalax sound across the world, and later serve in government.
In 1960 Senegal became independent, with Senghor as its first president.
Macky Sall, born in 1961, would be elected president in 2012 and serve until 2024.
In 1979 a race across the desert began, ending at Dakar, and the Dakar Rally made the city's name known worldwide.
Bassirou Diomaye Faye, born in 1980, would win the presidency in 2024.
The ferry Le Joola entered service in 1990. In 2002 it capsized off the Gambian coast, one of the worst disasters at sea in history.
Sadio Mane, born in 1992, would become one of Africa's finest footballers.
In 2008 work was under way on a giant bronze statue on a hill above Dakar, the African Renaissance Monument.
And in 2022, with Mane scoring the winning penalty, Senegal won the Africa Cup of Nations for the first time.
From the Jolof Empire to champions of Africa, Senegal's story goes on.
